packages.name: auditkit
packages.doc:
Package auditkit provides the shared audit-log infrastructure for Symaira
tools: a tamper-evident hash chain over JSONL entries and an append-only
file sink with size-based rotation.

Scope (deliberately narrow — no tool-specific logic):
  - HashEntry / VerifyChain: SHA-256 chaining over entry lines
  - ChainAnchor checkpoints (separate file, atomic replace) to detect
    truncation and authenticate the complete log for fast recovery —
    chaining alone only detects modification
  - Sink: append-only JSONL writer with rotation and fsync semantics

Domain models stay with the consumers: brain's redacting gateway logger
and guard's case bundles enrich the sink entries with their own schemas.

Standalone-first: standard library only.

declarations.name: AnchorSchemaVersion
declarations.doc: AnchorSchemaVersion is the current version of the ChainAnchor schema.

declarations.name: ChainAnchor
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.ChainAnchor struct{LastEntryHash string "json:\"last_entry_hash\""; EntryCount int64 "json:\"entry_count\""; SchemaVersion int "json:\"schema_version\""; LogSize int64 "json:\"log_size,omitempty\""; ContentHash string "json:\"content_hash,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc:
ChainAnchor is the external checkpoint for detecting audit-log truncation.
Hash-chaining alone detects modification of retained entries but not
deletion of the tail: an attacker with write access can drop the most
recent entries and the chain check over the remainder passes. The anchor
records the head hash and total count so a shortened log no longer
matches. Store it separately from the log file (different volume or
stricter permissions).

fields.name: ContentHash
fields.doc:
ContentHash authenticates the complete checkpointed log bytes. It keeps
the fast recovery path from trusting a same-size modified log.

fields.name: EntryCount
fields.doc: EntryCount is the total number of non-empty entries in the log.

fields.name: LastEntryHash
fields.doc: LastEntryHash is the SHA-256 of the most recent audit entry line.

fields.name: LogSize
fields.doc: LogSize is the exact byte size of the checkpointed log file.

fields.name: SchemaVersion
fields.doc: SchemaVersion for forward compatibility.

declarations.name: DefaultAnchorPath
declarations.doc:
DefaultAnchorPath returns the conventional anchor file path next to the
log file: <logPath>.anchor.

declarations.name: GenesisHash
declarations.doc: GenesisHash is the previous-hash value for the first entry in a chain.

declarations.name: HashEntry
declarations.doc:
HashEntry computes the SHA-256 chain hash of an audit entry line: the
previous entry's hash is mixed into the digest, so modifying any retained
entry breaks every subsequent link.

declarations.name: OpenSink
declarations.doc:
OpenSink opens (creating if needed) the JSONL audit file at path and
recovers the chain state by replaying existing lines.

declarations.name: ReadCheckpoint
declarations.doc:
ReadCheckpoint reads the anchor file. A missing anchor returns (nil, nil)
— there is no checkpoint yet, which callers treat as "unverified".

declarations.name: Sink
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.Sink struct{mu sync.Mutex; path string; maxBytes int64; file *os.File; writer *bufio.Writer; count int64; headHash string; degraded bool}
declarations.doc:
Sink is an append-only JSONL audit writer with size-based rotation.
It is safe for concurrent use. Every Append writes one line and flushes
it to the OS; the chain state (head hash, entry count) is tracked so
callers can checkpoint with WriteCheckpoint at any time.

methods.name: Append
methods.doc:
Append writes one JSONL line, updates the chain, and flushes.
The caller serializes its event payloads; Append does not validate the
content beyond requiring a single line (newlines are rejected so entries
stay one-per-line).

methods.name: Checkpoint
methods.doc: Checkpoint writes the anchor file for the current chain state.

methods.name: Close
methods.doc: Close flushes and closes the underlying file.

methods.name: Count
methods.doc: Count returns the number of entries written (including recovered ones).

methods.name: HeadHash
methods.doc: HeadHash returns the current chain head hash.

methods.name: Verify
methods.doc:
Verify audits the whole log file against the in-memory chain state and,
when present, the on-disk anchor.

declarations.name: SinkOption
declarations.doc: SinkOption configures a Sink.

declarations.name: Verification
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.Verification struct{Entries int64; HeadHash string; ChainOK bool; Anchored bool; AnchorOK bool; Truncated bool}
declarations.doc:
Verify reads back the log file and checks chain integrity plus the anchor
(when present). Returns the verification outcome; an absent anchor yields
Anchored=false rather than an error.

fields.name: AnchorOK
fields.doc: count + head match the checkpoint (truncation check)

fields.name: Anchored
fields.doc: an anchor file exists and was checked

fields.name: ChainOK
fields.doc: replayed chain matches the recorded head hash

fields.name: Entries
fields.doc: non-empty lines read back

fields.name: HeadHash
fields.doc: computed chain head over the file contents

fields.name: Truncated
fields.doc: anchored but count below checkpoint

declarations.name: VerifyAnchor
declarations.doc:
VerifyAnchor checks both that the entry count matches the checkpoint
(truncation detection) and that the chain validates (tamper detection).
A nil anchor fails closed.

declarations.name: VerifyAnchorForLog
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.VerifyAnchorForLog(entries []string, initialHash string, anchor *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.ChainAnchor, logSize int64, contentHash string) bool
declarations.doc:
VerifyAnchorForLog verifies the chain anchor and the byte-level identity of
the log. New anchors should use this stronger check; the older helper stays
compatible with anchors produced without a log path.

declarations.name: VerifyChain
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.VerifyChain(entries []string, initialHash string, expectedFinalHash string) bool
declarations.doc:
VerifyChain checks that entries form a valid hash chain from initialHash
(typically GenesisHash) to expectedFinalHash. Empty entries are skipped —
trailing newlines must not break verification.

declarations.name: WithMaxBytes
declarations.doc:
WithMaxBytes sets the rotation threshold (default: 10 MiB). When the log
exceeds it, it is renamed to <path>.1 (overwriting any previous .1) and a
fresh file starts. Rotation preserves chain verifiability per segment.

declarations.name: WriteCheckpoint
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.WriteCheckpoint(anchorPath string, hash string, count int64) error
declarations.doc:
WriteCheckpoint atomically writes the chain head to the anchor file
(write-to-temp then rename). The directory is created with 0700 if
missing; the anchor itself gets 0600.

declarations.name: WriteCheckpointForLog
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/auditkit.WriteCheckpointForLog(anchorPath string, logPath string, hash string, count int64) error
declarations.doc:
WriteCheckpointForLog writes an anchor that also authenticates the complete
log file, allowing recovery to skip JSONL replay while retaining tamper
detection. The legacy WriteCheckpoint API remains available for callers
that do not have a log path.

packages.name: configkit
packages.doc:
Package configkit provides generic TOML configuration loading with env var overrides.

Configuration is loaded in order of precedence (later overrides earlier):

 1. Defaults (from caller-provided function)
 2. Global TOML file ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/{appName}/config.toml, or
    ~/.config/{appName}/config.toml when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset)
 3. Project-local TOML file (./.{appName}.toml)
 4. Environment variables ({PREFIX}_{SECTION}_{FIELD})

Structs must use json tags for field name mapping:

	type MyConfig struct {
	    Server ServerConfig `json:"server"`
	}
	type ServerConfig struct {
	    Port int `json:"port"`
	}

The Loader type provides sync.Once caching (Load reads once, caches forever)
plus a Reload method for long-running servers that need hot config reload.

declarations.name: DefaultPath
declarations.doc:
DefaultPath returns the default global config file path for the given app name.
It honors XDG_CONFIG_HOME when it is set to an absolute path. Otherwise it
falls back to ~/.config. Example: DefaultPath("symfetch") →
"~/.config/symfetch/config.toml".

declarations.name: Loader
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/configkit.Loader[T any] struct{opts github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/configkit.Options; defaults func() *T; mu sync.RWMutex; once sync.Once; cached *T; cachedErr error}
declarations.doc:
Loader provides cached config loading for type T.
It implements sync.Once caching: Load reads from disk on the first call
and returns the cached value on subsequent calls. Use Reload for hot reload.
All cache state (once, cached, cachedErr) is guarded by mu, so Load,
Reload and ResetCache are safe to call concurrently.

methods.name: Load
methods.doc:
Load returns the config, loading and caching on first call.
Subsequent calls return the cached value without re-reading from disk.
Safe for concurrent use.

methods.name: Reload
methods.doc:
Reload reads a fresh config from disk (global + project + env vars),
bypassing the cache. Intended for long-running servers that need hot reload.
Safe for concurrent use.

methods.name: ResetCache
methods.doc:
ResetCache clears the cached config so the next Load reads from disk.
Intended for tests only. Safe for concurrent use.

declarations.name: NewLoader
declarations.doc: NewLoader creates a config loader. defaults returns a *T with sensible default values.

declarations.name: Options
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/configkit.Options struct{AppName string; EnvPrefix string; ConfigName string; UseLegacyConfigPath bool}
declarations.doc: Options configures the config loader.

fields.name: AppName
fields.doc:
AppName is the application name (e.g., "symfetch").
Used as the default env var prefix (uppercased) and config file name.

fields.name: ConfigName
fields.doc:
ConfigName overrides the config filename without extension.
Default: AppName. Global file: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/{ConfigName}/config.toml,
falling back to ~/.config/{ConfigName}/config.toml.
Project file: ./{ConfigName}.toml.

fields.name: EnvPrefix
fields.doc:
EnvPrefix overrides the env var prefix. Default: uppercase AppName.
For nested structs, env vars are named {PREFIX}_{SECTION}_{FIELD}.

fields.name: UseLegacyConfigPath
fields.doc:
UseLegacyConfigPath retains the pre-XDG behavior and always reads the
global file from ~/.config/{ConfigName}/config.toml. It is intended as a
temporary opt-out for consumers that need an explicit migration window.

packages.name: domkit
packages.doc:
Package domkit provides HTML parsing, Markdown rendering, and document
metadata extraction utilities for Symaira core tools.

The Markdown function converts HTML to LLM-optimized Markdown. The Render
function builds a full Document with URL, title, language, token-count
estimate, schema type, and optional content boundaries. The Outline
function extracts the heading structure (h1–h6) from a document.

Field names and frontmatter keys match the fetch-compatible output schema
used across the Symaira ecosystem (see testdata/fetch-schema.json for the
documented source of truth).
Package domkit provides the shared semantic DOM pipeline for the Symaira
fetch/browse family (issue X-3): HTML→Markdown rendering, outline
extraction, output schema, truncation and content-boundary markers.

The package is the extracted common core of the former
internal/render implementations in symaira-browse and symaira-fetch and
stays free of browser- and fingerprint-specific code.

declarations.name: Boundary
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Boundary struct{Nonce string "json:\"nonce\""; Origin string "json:\"origin\""; Start string "json:\"start\""; End string "json:\"end\""}
declarations.doc:
Boundary is the unforgeable content boundary marker (content-boundaries
contract). It is protocol-neutral so consumer tools (symbrowse, symfetch)
can attach it to rendered documents without importing each other.

methods.name: WrapText
methods.doc: WrapText wraps content between the boundary markers.

declarations.name: DefaultMaxChars
declarations.doc:
DefaultMaxChars is the per-page character budget for truncation. It matches
symfetch's default char_limit (15000).

declarations.name: Document
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Document struct{URL string "json:\"url\""; FinalURL string "json:\"final_url,omitempty\""; Title string "json:\"title,omitempty\""; Lang string "json:\"lang,omitempty\""; FetchedAt string "json:\"fetched_at\""; TokensEst int "json:\"tokens_est\""; SchemaType string "json:\"schema_type,omitempty\""; Markdown string "json:\"markdown,omitempty\""; Raw string "json:\"raw,omitempty\""; Outline []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Heading "json:\"outline,omitempty\""; Truncated bool "json:\"truncated\""; CharCount int "json:\"char_count\""; Meta github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.DocumentMeta "json:\"meta,omitempty\""; ContentBoundaries *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Boundary "json:\"content_boundaries,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc:
Document is the fetch-compatible read output. The metadata field names
(url, final_url, title, lang, fetched_at, tokens_est, schema_type) and the
frontmatter keys are identical to symfetch; the content fields (markdown,
outline, raw) are the browse-specific body carriers (see
testdata/fetch-schema.json). ContentBoundaries
carries the unforgeable boundary markers as an own JSON field when the
--content-boundaries flag is active.

declarations.name: DocumentMeta
declarations.doc:
DocumentMeta carries the fetch-style response metadata (subset of
symfetch's Meta with the same field names).

declarations.name: FetchedAtNow
declarations.doc:
FetchedAtNow returns the current UTC timestamp in the RFC3339 format
symfetch uses for fetched_at.

declarations.name: Frontmatter
declarations.doc:
Frontmatter renders the YAML metadata block with the exact key set and
ordering symfetch uses, followed by a blank line.

declarations.name: Heading
declarations.doc: Heading is one outline entry.

declarations.name: Lang
declarations.doc: Lang extracts the document language from the <html lang="…"> attribute.

declarations.name: Markdown
declarations.doc: Markdown converts an HTML document into LLM-optimized Markdown.

declarations.name: Options
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Options struct{Selector string; Filter string; Outline bool; Raw bool; MaxChars int}
declarations.doc: Options controls one read render.

fields.name: Filter
fields.doc: Filter removes every matching subtree before rendering.

fields.name: MaxChars
fields.doc: MaxChars is the truncation budget; zero means DefaultMaxChars.

fields.name: Outline
fields.doc: Outline returns only the heading structure.

fields.name: Raw
fields.doc: Raw returns the (possibly filtered/selected) HTML instead of Markdown.

fields.name: Selector
fields.doc: Selector restricts the render to the first matching subtree.

declarations.name: Outline
declarations.doc: Outline extracts the heading structure (h1–h6) of a document.

declarations.name: Render
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Render(pageHTML string, pageTitle string, pageURL string, options github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Options) (github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/domkit.Document, error)
declarations.doc:
Render builds the read document from raw page material. The page is
parsed exactly once; the parsed tree is shared by language detection,
schema extraction, outline and markdown rendering. The exported
string-based helpers (Lang, Markdown, Outline) parse independently for
direct callers.

declarations.name: StripBase64Images
declarations.doc:
StripBase64Images replaces inline base64-encoded image data in Markdown
and HTML content with lightweight [IMAGE: alt] placeholders.
Real image URLs (http/https) are preserved unchanged.
The function is safe for content of any size (runs in linear time).

declarations.name: Truncate
declarations.doc:
Truncate applies symfetch's truncate-and-store window semantics to a body:
when the rune count exceeds maxChars the head and tail halves of the budget
are kept and the omitted middle is marked. The result reports whether the
body was truncated. (Persisting the full text to the cache is owned by the
token-budget issue, B-19.)

packages.name: envutil
packages.doc: Package envutil provides environment variable helpers with fallback support.

declarations.name: Getenv
declarations.doc:
Getenv returns the value of the primary environment variable. If the primary
is empty or unset, it tries each legacy alias in order and returns the first
non-empty value found. Returns "" if none are set.

declarations.name: Unsetenv
declarations.doc:
Unsetenv removes the named environment variable from the environment.
It is a thin wrapper around os.Unsetenv that returns any error.

packages.name: evidencekit
packages.doc:
Package evidencekit defines Symaira-wide grounded extraction contracts:
a source reference, a character span, and an Extraction that ties an
extracted fact back to the exact source text that justified it.

The pattern: callers align EvidenceText against the original source text
to produce a Span. Alignment can be exact (byte-identical substring),
normalized (whitespace-collapsed substring), or fuzzy (token-based
approximate match); when none succeeds the extraction is marked
AlignmentUnmatched and must not be treated as grounded by consumers that
require grounded-only ingestion.

This package has no cloud, LLM, or tool-specific dependencies and does not
import symingest, symseek, or symmemory. It only defines the shared shape
and the deterministic alignment/validation helpers around it.

declarations.name: Align
declarations.doc:
Align tries AlignExact, then AlignNormalized, then a token-based fuzzy
fallback (AlignFuzzy), and reports the resulting Span alongside the
AlignmentStatus that produced it. When no strategy succeeds it returns a
zero Span and AlignmentUnmatched.

declarations.name: AlignExact
declarations.doc:
AlignExact reports whether evidenceText occurs verbatim in source and, if
so, returns its byte span.

declarations.name: AlignFuzzy
declarations.doc:
AlignFuzzy reports whether evidenceText approximately occurs in source
using pure-stdlib text processing: both sides are split into
whitespace-separated tokens, a sliding window of source tokens (sized len(evidence
tokens)-1..+1) is scored with an LCS-style sequence matcher where tokens
match when identical or within a small edit-distance ratio, and the best
window wins when its similarity is at least fuzzyMinScore. The returned
Span maps back to byte offsets in the original source.

declarations.name: AlignNormalized
declarations.doc:
AlignNormalized reports whether evidenceText occurs in source once runs of
whitespace are collapsed to a single space on both sides (and the
evidence text is trimmed). The returned Span maps back to byte offsets in
the original, un-normalized source.

declarations.name: AlignmentExact
declarations.doc:
AlignmentExact means EvidenceText was found as a byte-identical
substring of the source text.

declarations.name: AlignmentFuzzy
declarations.doc:
AlignmentFuzzy means EvidenceText was located only by the
token-based fuzzy fallback: a token sliding-window over the source
scored by sequence similarity (LCS-style, difflib-like) with
per-token edit-distance tolerance. It runs only after exact and
whitespace-normalized matching fail. Validate rejects fuzzy
alignments by default; see ValidateWithOptions.

declarations.name: AlignmentNormalized
declarations.doc:
AlignmentNormalized means EvidenceText was found only after
collapsing runs of whitespace in both source and evidence text.

declarations.name: AlignmentStatus
declarations.doc:
AlignmentStatus describes how confidently an Extraction's EvidenceText was
located in its source text. Field values are part of the cross-repo
contract — do not rename.

declarations.name: AlignmentUnmatched
declarations.doc:
AlignmentUnmatched means EvidenceText could not be located in the
source text by any supported strategy. Span is meaningless and
callers requiring grounded-only ingestion must reject or downgrade
the extraction.

declarations.name: DecodeJSONL
declarations.doc:
DecodeJSONL reads newline-delimited Extraction JSON from r. Blank lines
are skipped.

declarations.name: EncodeJSONL
declarations.doc:
EncodeJSONL writes extractions to w as newline-delimited JSON, one
Extraction per line — the extraction sidecar format shared across repos.

declarations.name: ErrEmptyEvidence
declarations.doc: ErrEmptyEvidence marks an Extraction with empty EvidenceText.

declarations.name: ErrInvalidSpan
declarations.doc:
ErrInvalidSpan marks an Extraction whose Span has negative or
decreasing bounds.

declarations.name: ErrUnmatched
declarations.doc:
ErrUnmatched marks an Extraction whose EvidenceText could not be
located in the source text by any alignment strategy.

declarations.name: Extraction
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/evidencekit.Extraction struct{Source github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/evidencekit.SourceRef "json:\"source\""; Text string "json:\"text\""; EvidenceText string "json:\"evidence_text\""; Span github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/evidencekit.Span "json:\"span\""; AlignmentStatus github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/evidencekit.AlignmentStatus "json:\"alignment_status\""; Attributes map[string]string "json:\"attributes,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc:
Extraction is one grounded fact extracted from a source, together with
the evidence text and its span in the source text. Field names are part
of the cross-repo JSON contract — do not rename.

declarations.name: SourceRef
declarations.doc:
SourceRef identifies the source document, session, or record that an
Extraction's evidence was drawn from. Field names are part of the
cross-repo JSON contract (snake_case) — do not rename.

declarations.name: Span
declarations.doc: Span is a half-open [Start, End) byte range into the source text.

declarations.name: Validate
declarations.doc:
Validate checks that an Extraction is grounded: its AlignmentStatus is
AlignmentExact or AlignmentNormalized (strict by default — fuzzy
alignments are rejected; see ValidateWithOptions), its EvidenceText is
non-empty, and its Span has non-negative, non-decreasing bounds. Callers
implementing grounded-only ingestion should reject any Extraction that
fails Validate.

Returned errors wrap ErrUnmatched, ErrEmptyEvidence, or ErrInvalidSpan
(see errors.Is).

declarations.name: ValidateOptions
declarations.doc: ValidateOptions tunes Validate. The zero value is strict validation.

fields.name: AcceptFuzzy
fields.doc:
AcceptFuzzy allows extractions whose AlignmentStatus is
AlignmentFuzzy. By default Validate rejects fuzzy alignments as
not grounded.

declarations.name: ValidateWithOptions
declarations.doc: ValidateWithOptions is Validate with caller-supplied options.

packages.name: exitcodes
packages.doc: Package exitcodes provides standardized CLI exit codes and structured error types for the Symaira ecosystem.

declarations.name: CLIError
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.CLIError struct{Code github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.ExitCode; Kind github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.ErrorKind; Message string; Cause error; Hint string}
declarations.doc:
CLIError is a structured error with an exit code, kind classification,
user-friendly message, optional wrapped cause, and optional remediation hint.

methods.name: Error
methods.doc: Error implements the error interface.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc: Unwrap returns the underlying cause for errors.Is/errors.As support.

declarations.name: ErrorKind
declarations.doc: ErrorKind categorizes CLI errors for programmatic handling and display.

declarations.name: ExitCode
declarations.doc:
ExitCode represents a process exit code for CLI commands.

The exit codes follow a convention inspired by sysexits.h but adapted for
the Symaira ecosystem. New categories MUST be added at the end of the block
to preserve backward compatibility with scripts that match on numeric codes.

declarations.name: ExitCodeFromError
declarations.doc:
ExitCodeFromError extracts the exit code from an error.
If err is nil, it returns ExitOK.
If err wraps a *CLIError, it returns that error's code.
Otherwise it returns ExitGeneric.

declarations.name: ExitConfig
declarations.doc: ExitConfig indicates a configuration error.

declarations.name: ExitConflict
declarations.doc:
ExitConflict indicates a conflict with the current state (e.g. resource
already exists or version mismatch).

declarations.name: ExitData
declarations.doc: ExitData indicates an error in the data format or content.

declarations.name: ExitForbidden
declarations.doc:
ExitForbidden indicates the operation was permitted but not allowed
(insufficient permissions).

declarations.name: ExitGeneric
declarations.doc: ExitGeneric indicates a general or unspecified error.

declarations.name: ExitInterrupted
declarations.doc: ExitInterrupted indicates the operation was interrupted.

declarations.name: ExitNoAuth
declarations.doc: ExitNoAuth indicates an authentication failure (bad credentials, missing token).

declarations.name: ExitNoInput
declarations.doc: ExitNoInput indicates that input was missing or required but not provided.

declarations.name: ExitNotFound
declarations.doc: ExitNotFound indicates the requested resource was not found.

declarations.name: ExitOK
declarations.doc: ExitOK indicates successful completion.

declarations.name: ExitSoftware
declarations.doc: ExitSoftware indicates an internal software error (bug).

declarations.name: FormatCLIError
declarations.doc:
FormatCLIError formats an error for human-readable CLI output.
If the error is a *CLIError with a non-empty Hint, the hint is appended
on a separate line prefixed with "Hint: ".
If the error has a Cause, the full chain is shown.
If the error is not a *CLIError, the default error string is returned.

declarations.name: KindAuth
declarations.doc: KindAuth indicates an authentication error.

declarations.name: KindConfig
declarations.doc: KindConfig indicates a configuration error.

declarations.name: KindConflict
declarations.doc: KindConflict indicates a state conflict.

declarations.name: KindInternal
declarations.doc: KindInternal indicates an internal error.

declarations.name: KindNotFound
declarations.doc: KindNotFound indicates the resource was not found.

declarations.name: KindPermission
declarations.doc: KindPermission indicates a permission/authorization error.

declarations.name: KindUnavailable
declarations.doc: KindUnavailable indicates the resource or service is unavailable.

declarations.name: KindValidation
declarations.doc: KindValidation indicates an input validation error.

declarations.name: Wrap
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.Wrap(err error, code github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.ExitCode, kind github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.ErrorKind, msg string) *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.CLIError
declarations.doc: Wrap creates a new CLIError wrapping the given cause with a message string.

declarations.name: Wrapf
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.Wrapf(err error, code github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.ExitCode, kind github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.ErrorKind, format string, args ...any) *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/exitcodes.CLIError
declarations.doc: Wrapf creates a new CLIError wrapping the given cause with a formatted message.

packages.name: fsutil
packages.doc: Package fsutil provides safe filesystem operations including atomic writes and path validation.

declarations.name: AtomicWriteFile
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/fsutil.AtomicWriteFile(path string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error
declarations.doc:
AtomicWriteFile writes data to a unique temporary file in the same directory,
fsyncs it, closes it, and then atomically renames it to path. This prevents
partial writes or crashes from leaving the target file in an inconsistent
state and avoids temp file name collisions under concurrency.

declarations.name: ErrInvalidPath
declarations.doc: ErrInvalidPath is returned when a path contains invalid characters or patterns.

declarations.name: HasTraversal
declarations.doc: HasTraversal reports whether path contains an explicit parent-directory segment.

declarations.name: SafeMkdirAll
declarations.doc:
SafeMkdirAll creates a directory at path and all necessary parent directories,
hardening against symlink-traversal attacks. Each existing path component is
checked with Lstat — symlinks owned by non-root are rejected (they are outside
the system trust boundary, e.g. an attacker placing a symlink inside a
user-writable directory). Root-owned symlinks (e.g. /var → /private/var
on macOS) are trusted and resolved via EvalSymlinks so the remaining path is
created at the real location.

declarations.name: SafeWriteFile
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/fsutil.SafeWriteFile(path string, data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error

declarations.name: ValidatePath
declarations.doc:
ValidatePath validates a file path for safety.
It rejects paths containing:
  - Parent directory traversal (..)
  - Null bytes (\x00)
  - Control characters (< 0x20), including tab and newline
  - Absolute paths
  - Empty segments (double slashes)

Returns nil if the path is valid, or an error describing the specific issue.

packages.name: llmkit
packages.doc:
Package llmkit provides the shared LLM provider layer for the Symaira Go
tools, implementing docs/llm-provider-contract.md.

The design is one HTTP transport plus a dialect table: almost every vendor
speaks the OpenAI wire format, so adding a provider is a descriptor entry in
contracts/llm_providers.json rather than new client code. Anthropic is the
only genuine wire exception. Custom endpoints and local servers (Ollama,
llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM) are ordinary descriptors with a base-URL
override.

Credentials are resolved through the shared reference format
(symvault://, keychain://, env://NAME) — the client never takes a raw key
from config files. Errors are classified into the six-category contract
taxonomy and map onto corekit exitcodes values, so callers branch on codes
instead of string-matching upstream text.

This package has no cloud or tool-specific dependencies and imports no
sibling Symaira tool beyond this module's own exitcodes package.

declarations.name: AsError
declarations.doc:
AsError extracts a *Error from err, or nil when err is not a classified
provider failure.

declarations.name: AuthBearer
declarations.doc: AuthBearer sends "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

declarations.name: AuthHeader
declarations.doc: AuthHeader sends the key in a named header (e.g. x-api-key).

declarations.name: AuthNone
declarations.doc: AuthNone sends no credential (local servers).

declarations.name: AuthScheme
declarations.doc: AuthScheme identifies how a request carries credentials.

declarations.name: Capabilities
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Capabilities struct{Streaming bool "json:\"streaming\""; ToolUse bool "json:\"tool_use\""; Embeddings bool "json:\"embeddings\""; Vision bool "json:\"vision\""; SystemPrompt bool "json:\"system_prompt\""}
declarations.doc:
Capabilities are the feature promises a descriptor makes. A consumer must
not offer a feature the descriptor does not promise.

declarations.name: ChatOptions
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ChatOptions struct{Temperature *float64; MaxTokens int; System string; Tools []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Tool; ResponseFormat encoding/json.RawMessage}
declarations.doc: ChatOptions carries optional per-request parameters.

fields.name: ResponseFormat
fields.doc:
ResponseFormat constrains the model output on OpenAI-wire endpoints
(response_format body field). Consumers that must parse structured
output pass the provider's JSON-schema shape here, e.g. the OpenAI
object {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{...}}. Anthropic-wire
endpoints ignore it.

fields.name: System
fields.doc: convenience system prompt; merged into messages

fields.name: Tools
fields.doc: requires the provider's tool_use capability

declarations.name: ChatStreamResponse
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ChatStreamResponse struct{Model string "json:\"model\""; Message github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Message "json:\"message\""; Done bool "json:\"done\""}
declarations.doc: ChatStreamResponse is one chunk from a streaming native /api/chat call.

declarations.name: Choice
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Choice struct{Content string "json:\"content\""; ToolCalls []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ToolCall "json:\"tool_calls,omitempty\""; FinishReason string "json:\"finish_reason,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc: Choice is the assistant's response to a chat request.

declarations.name: Client
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client struct{desc github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Descriptor; baseURL string; dialect github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.WireDialect; apiKey string; extraHdr map[string]string; http *net/http.Client}
declarations.doc:
Client is an HTTP client for one provider descriptor. It is safe for
concurrent use once constructed.

methods.name: BaseURL
methods.doc: BaseURL returns the resolved base URL.

methods.name: Chat
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).Chat(ctx context.Context, model string, messages []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Message, opts *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ChatOptions) (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Choice, error)
methods.doc: Chat performs a non-streaming chat completion and returns the first choice.

methods.name: ChatStream
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).ChatStream(ctx context.Context, model string, messages []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Message, callback func(github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ChatStreamResponse) error) error
methods.doc: ChatStream streams a native Ollama chat completion.

methods.name: ChatStreamWithOptions
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).ChatStreamWithOptions(ctx context.Context, model string, messages []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Message, callback func(github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ChatStreamResponse) error, opts ...github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.NativeChatOption) error
methods.doc:
ChatStreamWithOptions streams a native Ollama chat completion with optional
request parameters.

methods.name: Descriptor
methods.doc: Descriptor returns the provider descriptor this client was built from.

methods.name: Embed
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).Embed(ctx context.Context, model string, inputs []string, opts ...github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.EmbedOption) ([]github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Embedding, error)
methods.doc:
Embed returns embeddings for inputs via the OpenAI /embeddings wire format.
Requires the provider's embeddings capability.

methods.name: EmbedNative
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).EmbedNative(ctx context.Context, model string, inputs []string, dimensions int) ([][]float32, error)
methods.doc:
EmbedNative returns embeddings through Ollama's native /api/embed endpoint.
A zero dimensions value omits the optional dimensions field.

methods.name: Generate
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).Generate(ctx context.Context, model string, prompt string, callback func(github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.GenerateResponse) error, opts ...github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.GenerateOption) error
methods.doc:
Generate streams a native Ollama text generation. The callback receives one
chunk per line of the NDJSON stream.

methods.name: ListModels
methods.doc:
ListModels resolves the model list for this client's provider. Static lists
come from the descriptor; discovered lists are fetched live (OpenRouter
/models, Ollama /api/tags).

methods.name: ListOllamaModels
methods.doc: ListOllamaModels returns native Ollama model metadata.

methods.name: Ping
methods.doc: Ping checks whether the local Ollama server answers.

methods.name: StreamChat
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Client).StreamChat(ctx context.Context, model string, messages []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Message, opts *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ChatOptions, callback func(delta string) error, streamOpts ...github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.StreamOption) error
methods.doc:
StreamChat performs a streaming chat completion, invoking callback for each
content delta. Requires the provider's streaming capability.

declarations.name: DefaultTimeout
declarations.doc: DefaultTimeout is the default per-request timeout.

declarations.name: Descriptor
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Descriptor struct{ID string "json:\"id\""; DisplayName string "json:\"display_name\""; BaseURL string "json:\"base_url\""; BaseURLOverridable bool "json:\"base_url_overridable\""; BaseURLRequiredOverride bool "json:\"base_url_required_override,omitempty\""; AuthScheme github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.AuthScheme "json:\"auth_scheme\""; AuthHeader string "json:\"auth_header,omitempty\""; ExtraHeaders map[string]string "json:\"extra_headers,omitempty\""; Dialect github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.WireDialect "json:\"dialect\""; DialectConfigurable bool "json:\"dialect_configurable,omitempty\""; Capabilities github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Capabilities "json:\"capabilities\""; Models github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ModelSource "json:\"models\""; CredentialEnvDefault string "json:\"credential_env_default,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc:
Descriptor is the declarative description of one LLM provider. It mirrors
the entries in contracts/llm_providers.json; see the contract document for
field semantics.

methods.name: DefaultModel
methods.doc: DefaultModel returns the descriptor's fallback model, if any.

methods.name: Validate
methods.doc:
Validate reports whether the descriptor is usable as configured: a base URL
exists (or an override is supplied separately) and the dialect is known.

declarations.name: DialectAnthropic
declarations.doc: DialectAnthropic is the Anthropic messages wire format.

declarations.name: DialectOpenAI
declarations.doc:
DialectOpenAI is the OpenAI chat-completions wire format, spoken by
most vendors and local servers.

declarations.name: EmbedOption
declarations.doc: EmbedOption configures an embeddings call.

declarations.name: Embedding
declarations.doc: Embedding is one embedding vector with the model that produced it.

declarations.name: ErrCodeAuth
declarations.doc: ErrCodeAuth means the credential is missing, invalid or expired.

declarations.name: ErrCodeContextOverflow
declarations.doc: ErrCodeContextOverflow means the prompt exceeds the context window.

declarations.name: ErrCodeModelNotFound
declarations.doc:
ErrCodeModelNotFound means the model/deployment does not exist for
this credential.

declarations.name: ErrCodeProvider
declarations.doc: ErrCodeProvider means any other provider-reported failure.

declarations.name: ErrCodeRateLimited
declarations.doc:
ErrCodeRateLimited means the provider rejected the request for rate
limiting; RetryAfter may carry the reported delay.

declarations.name: ErrCodeTransport
declarations.doc:
ErrCodeTransport means a network-level failure (refused, DNS, TLS,
timeout).

declarations.name: Error
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Error struct{Code github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ErrorCode; StatusCode int; Body string; RetryAfter string; Err error}
declarations.doc:
Error is a classified provider failure. Use errors.As to extract it from a
call chain; ExitCode maps the failure onto the shared CLI exit-code table.

methods.name: ExitCode
methods.doc: ExitCode maps this failure onto the exitcodes table per the contract.

methods.name: RetryAfterSeconds
methods.doc:
RetryAfterSeconds parses the seconds form of the provider's Retry-After
value. It returns false when the value is absent or unparseable.

methods.name: Retryable
methods.doc: Retryable reports whether retrying the same request can plausibly succeed.

fields.name: Body
fields.doc: upstream body excerpt, truncated

fields.name: Err
fields.doc: underlying transport error, if any

fields.name: RetryAfter
fields.doc: provider-reported retry delay, rate-limited only

fields.name: StatusCode
fields.doc: upstream HTTP status, 0 for transport failures

declarations.name: ErrorCode
declarations.doc:
ErrorCode is the contract error taxonomy from
contracts/llm_errors.json. Callers branch on these codes instead of
string-matching provider-specific error text.

declarations.name: GenerateOption
declarations.doc: GenerateOption configures a native /api/generate call.

declarations.name: GenerateResponse
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.GenerateResponse struct{Model string "json:\"model\""; Response string "json:\"response\""; Done bool "json:\"done\""}
declarations.doc: GenerateResponse is one chunk from a streaming native /api/generate call.

declarations.name: Lookup
declarations.doc: Lookup returns the descriptor with the given id.

declarations.name: Message
declarations.doc: Message is one turn in a chat conversation.

fields.name: Role
fields.doc: "system", "user", "assistant", "tool"

declarations.name: ModelInfo
declarations.doc: ModelInfo describes one discovered or static model.

declarations.name: ModelSource
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ModelSource struct{Mode string "json:\"mode\""; DiscoveryPath string "json:\"discovery_path,omitempty\""; Default string "json:\"default\""}
declarations.doc: ModelSource describes how the model list for a provider is obtained.

fields.name: Default
fields.doc: Default is the fallback model ID, possibly empty.

fields.name: DiscoveryPath
fields.doc:
DiscoveryPath is the endpoint to query when Mode is "discovered",
interpreted against the provider root (see Descriptor.DiscoveryURL).

fields.name: Mode
fields.doc: Mode is one of "static", "discovered", "deployment", "configured".

declarations.name: NativeChatOption
declarations.doc: NativeChatOption configures a native Ollama chat request.

declarations.name: NewClient
declarations.doc:
NewClient builds a Client for desc. The credential is resolved through the
shared reference format: symvault://, keychain://, env://NAME, or a bare
environment-variable name. Descriptors with auth scheme "none" skip
resolution entirely.

declarations.name: OllamaModelInfo
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.OllamaModelInfo struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; Modified string "json:\"modified_at\""; Size int64 "json:\"size\""}
declarations.doc:
OllamaModelInfo is the native metadata returned by Ollama's /api/tags
endpoint. It is separate from ModelInfo so generic provider JSON contracts
do not gain Ollama-specific fields.

declarations.name: Option
declarations.doc: Option configures a Client at construction time.

declarations.name: Providers
declarations.doc: Providers returns every descriptor in the shared registry.

declarations.name: ResolveCredential
declarations.doc:
ResolveCredential resolves a credential reference in the shared format:

	symvault://path  -> `symvault get -- path --print`
	keychain://svc/acct -> reserved for Swift consumers; unsupported here
	env://NAME       -> os.Getenv("NAME")
	NAME             -> bare env name shorthand for env://NAME

An empty ref falls back to envDefault (a bare env name). The resolved value
must never be logged; errors name only the reference.

Deprecated: the resolution logic now lives in [secretref.Resolve], the
shared implementation used across the Symaira Go tools. This forwarder is
kept so existing llmkit callers do not need to change; keychain:// stays
refused here exactly as before — llmkit itself has no Swift-side identity,
so it never attempts the macOS-only resolution secretref now offers.

declarations.name: StreamOption
declarations.doc: StreamOption configures a streaming chat call.

declarations.name: Tool
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.Tool struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; Description string "json:\"description,omitempty\""; InputSchema encoding/json.RawMessage "json:\"parameters,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc:
Tool is a function the model may call, in OpenAI tool-use shape. Anthropic
tools are converted at request time.

declarations.name: ToolCall
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/llmkit.ToolCall struct{ID string "json:\"id\""; Name string "json:\"name\""; Arguments encoding/json.RawMessage "json:\"arguments\""}
declarations.doc: ToolCall is one tool invocation requested by the model.

fields.name: Arguments
fields.doc: JSON object

declarations.name: WireDialect
declarations.doc: WireDialect names a request/response wire format.

declarations.name: WithAPIKey
declarations.doc:
WithAPIKey supplies the credential directly, bypassing the shared
reference resolution. Used by consumers that hold their own secret
store (keychain, vault integrations) and only need llmkit for the
wire transport.

declarations.name: WithBaseURL
declarations.doc:
WithBaseURL overrides the descriptor's default endpoint (only valid when
the descriptor declares base_url_overridable or requires an override).

declarations.name: WithDialect
declarations.doc: WithDialect overrides the wire dialect (custom endpoints only).

declarations.name: WithEmbedDimensions
declarations.doc:
WithEmbedDimensions pins the output dimension via the OpenAI-wire
`dimensions` body field (Matryoshka truncation). 0 means the provider
default dimension.

declarations.name: WithGenerateFormat
declarations.doc:
WithGenerateFormat constrains the generated output to a JSON-schema
object (Ollama `format` field). Pass the schema itself, e.g. the
consolidation schema consumers send for structured replies.

declarations.name: WithGenerateFormatValue
declarations.doc:
WithGenerateFormatValue sets Ollama's format field to either "json" or a
JSON-schema object. It exists for compatibility with the legacy ollamakit
API while retaining the typed schema helper above.

declarations.name: WithGenerateImages
declarations.doc: WithGenerateImages sets the base64-encoded images sent to a vision model.

declarations.name: WithGenerateSystem
declarations.doc: WithGenerateSystem sets the system prompt on a native generate call.

declarations.name: WithGenerateTemperature
declarations.doc: WithGenerateTemperature sets the native Ollama sampling temperature.

declarations.name: WithHTTPClient
declarations.doc: WithHTTPClient supplies a custom *http.Client (tests, transports).

declarations.name: WithNativeChatFormat
declarations.doc: WithNativeChatFormat sets Ollama's JSON response mode.

declarations.name: WithNativeChatTemperature
declarations.doc: WithNativeChatTemperature sets the native Ollama sampling temperature.

declarations.name: WithStreamFinished
declarations.doc:
WithStreamFinished registers a callback invoked when the provider signals
the terminal finish/stop reason of the stream (e.g. "max_tokens",
"stop", "tool_calls"). The callback is called at most once; when the
provider never reports a reason it is not called.

declarations.name: WithTimeout
declarations.doc: WithTimeout sets the per-request timeout.

packages.name: main
packages.doc:
Command gen regenerates llmkit/providers.json from the shared contract
source of truth in contracts/llm_providers.json. Run it whenever the
contract registry changes:

	go generate ./llmkit/   (or: go run ./llmkit/gen)

packages.name: logkit
packages.doc: Package logkit provides structured logging helpers for CLI applications.

declarations.name: Default
declarations.doc:
Default returns the package-default structured logger configured via
environment variables. It is safe for concurrent use.

The env prefix is the app name passed to InitDefault (uppercased); if
InitDefault was not called it falls back to the neutral "SYM" prefix:
  - {PREFIX}_LOG_LEVEL: debug, info, warn, error (default: warn)
  - {PREFIX}_LOG_FORMAT: text (default), json

declarations.name: InitDefault
declarations.doc:
InitDefault sets the application name that Default() uses to read its
environment configuration. Call it once at program startup, before the first
Default() call. It resets any previously constructed default logger so the
next Default() call rebuilds it with the new prefix.

For example, InitDefault("symfetch") makes Default() read SYMFETCH_LOG_LEVEL
and SYMFETCH_LOG_FORMAT.

declarations.name: New
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/logkit.New(w io.Writer, level log/slog.Level, format string) *log/slog.Logger
declarations.doc:
New creates a slog.Logger with the specified writer, level and format.
Format must be "text" or "json".

declarations.name: NewFromEnv
declarations.doc:
NewFromEnv creates a fresh slog.Logger by reading environment variables
prefixed with the given appName. For example, NewFromEnv("symfetch")
reads SYMFETCH_LOG_LEVEL and SYMFETCH_LOG_FORMAT.

declarations.name: ReplaceLogger
declarations.doc:
ReplaceLogger allows tests to swap the default logger.
The returned function restores the previous logger.

packages.name: mcpcfgkit
packages.doc:
Package mcpcfgkit provides MCP server config discovery across AI client
applications. It is the shared implementation behind symscope's mcpcfg,
symguard's discovery, and symbrain's harness config handling: JSONC/JSON/
YAML config parsing, client source enumeration, and a testable FS
abstraction.

Scope (deliberately narrow — no tool-specific logic):
  - Client sources (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, …) with env-aware
    path resolution
  - mcpServers config parsing from JSONC / JSON / YAML
  - Server model with transport/command/args/env, ready for consumers to
    enrich with tool-specific fields

Standalone-first: this package imports no other Symaira module and depends
only on the standard library + gopkg.in/yaml.v3.

declarations.name: Client
declarations.doc: Client identifies a supported AI client application.

declarations.name: DefaultSources
declarations.doc:
DefaultSources returns the well-known client config locations for the
current platform and user. Missing files are tolerated by scan/discover.

declarations.name: DefaultSourcesForPlatform
declarations.doc:
DefaultSourcesForPlatform is the injectable variant of [DefaultSources] so
consumers can test platform-specific path resolution (darwin vs linux XDG)
deterministically on any host.

declarations.name: Discover
declarations.doc:
Discover scans the given sources and returns the configured servers plus
non-fatal notes (unreadable files, missing keys, parse errors).

declarations.name: Entry
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.Entry struct{Command string "json:\"command,omitempty\""; Args []string "json:\"args,omitempty\""; URL string "json:\"url,omitempty\""; Type string "json:\"type,omitempty\""; Transport string "json:\"transport,omitempty\""; Env map[string]string "json:\"env,omitempty\""; Environment map[string]string "json:\"environment,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc: Entry is one raw server entry inside the config map.

methods.name: CommandOrURL
methods.doc:
CommandOrURL returns the launch command for stdio servers or the URL for
remote ones — the single field guard's Server collapses both into Command.

methods.name: MergedEnv
methods.doc:
MergedEnv returns env merged with environment ("environment" wins on
conflicts), mirroring OpenCode's dual-key layout.

methods.name: TransportValue
methods.doc:
TransportValue resolves the effective transport from URL/type/transport
fields. OpenCode's "local"/"remote" types map to stdio/http.

fields.name: Environment
fields.doc: Environment is OpenCode's alternative env key ("environment").

declarations.name: FS
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.FS interface{Glob(pattern string) ([]string, error); ReadFile(path string) ([]byte, error)}
declarations.doc:
FS abstracts filesystem access so tests can inject fixtures without
touching real client configs.

declarations.name: Finding
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.Finding struct{Client github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.Client; Path string; Status github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.Status; Message string}
declarations.doc:
Finding reports a client config source (or an entry within it) that could
not be mapped exactly. It names the client, the source path, a status, and
a human-readable message.

declarations.name: JSONCStrip
declarations.doc:
JSONCStrip removes // line comments and /* block comments from JSONC text,
preserving strings (so URLs like "https://" survive) and their escapes.
This is the minimal scanner shared by all MCP-config consumers.

declarations.name: OSFS
declarations.doc: OSFS is the real filesystem implementation.

declarations.name: ScanAll
declarations.doc:
ScanAll scans all well-known clients and returns a ScanResult. Every
client source that cannot be scanned — missing file, unreadable file, or
parse failure — is reported as a Finding; nothing is skipped silently.

declarations.name: ScanAllWithFS
declarations.doc:
ScanAllWithFS is like ScanAll but uses the provided FS and sources, making
it straightforward to test.

declarations.name: ScanResult
declarations.doc:
ScanResult is the outcome of a discovery scan: the normalised servers that
could be mapped, plus findings for every source or entry that could not.

declarations.name: ScanSource
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.ScanSource struct{Client github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.Client; Path string; Key string}
declarations.doc:
ScanSource pairs a client identifier with its config path and the top-level
key holding the servers map (empty Key means "mcpServers").

declarations.name: Server
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpcfgkit.Server struct{Name string "json:\"name\""; Client string "json:\"client\""; Transport string "json:\"transport\""; Command string "json:\"command,omitempty\""; Args []string "json:\"args,omitempty\""; URL string "json:\"url,omitempty\""; ConfigPath string "json:\"config_path,omitempty\""; Env map[string]string "json:\"env,omitempty\""; EnvKeys []string "json:\"-\""; EnvValues []string "json:\"-\""}
declarations.doc:
Server is one configured MCP server entry. Consumers enrich this with
tool-specific fields (credential warnings, secret-backed flags, …).

fields.name: EnvKeys
fields.doc:
EnvKeys/EnvValues hold the environment variables split into keys and
values so callers can redact values while keeping key visibility.

fields.name: Transport
fields.doc: stdio | http | sse

declarations.name: Source
declarations.doc:
Source is the simpler V1 alias of ScanSource (plain-string client field)
kept for the Discover convenience API. It shares the same layout so both
APIs can share internals.

declarations.name: Status
declarations.doc:
Status describes how completely a client's MCP configuration source was
mapped during a scan.

declarations.name: StatusApproximate
declarations.doc: StatusApproximate means the source was mapped with assumptions.

declarations.name: StatusExact
declarations.doc: StatusExact means the source was fully mapped to server entries.

declarations.name: StatusManual
declarations.doc: StatusManual means the source requires manual review.

declarations.name: StatusUnsupported
declarations.doc: StatusUnsupported means the source could not be mapped at all.

declarations.name: Transport
declarations.doc: Transport describes how a server is reached.

packages.name: mcpserver
packages.doc:
Package mcpserver provides a JSON-RPC 2.0 server framework for the Model
Context Protocol (MCP). It implements the MCP stdio transport with
Content-Length framing and exposes a registration-based API so that
consumers can define tools without coupling to the protocol layer.

declarations.name: ContentBlock
declarations.doc:
ContentBlock is one MCP tool-result content item. It intentionally accepts
arbitrary JSON fields so consumers can return text, image, audio,
resource-link, or embedded-resource blocks without the corekit needing to
model every MCP content variant.

declarations.name: New
declarations.doc: New creates a new MCP server.

declarations.name: RegisterTyped
declarations.signature: func github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.RegisterTyped[T any](srv *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.Server, name string, description string, handler func(context.Context, T) (any, error))
declarations.doc:
RegisterTyped registers a tool whose input schema is derived from the Go
type T and whose handler receives the raw "arguments" object unmarshalled
into T. It is an additive convenience over the raw Tool{InputSchema,
Handler} path, which keeps working unchanged.

Schema derivation rules:
  - T must be a struct (or a pointer to a struct); the resulting schema is
    always of type "object".
  - Field names come from the `json` tag (the part before the first comma),
    falling back to the field name. Fields tagged `json:"-"` and unexported
    fields are skipped.
  - A `desc` tag provides the property's "description".
  - A field is "required" unless it is a pointer type or its json tag
    carries `omitempty`.
  - Supported field kinds: string, bool, all int/uint sizes (integer),
    float32/float64 (number), slices (array, item schema derived
    recursively), nested structs and pointers to structs (object), and
    json.RawMessage (opaque). Unsupported kinds cause RegisterTyped to
    panic, mirroring RegisterTool's panic-on-misuse contract.

Dispatch policy: arguments are decoded with DisallowUnknownFields, so
clients sending properties outside the derived schema get a descriptive
tool error instead of silently dropped data. Bad JSON is likewise reported
as a tool error.

declarations.name: RequestMeta
declarations.doc:
RequestMeta returns the optional _meta object supplied with tools/call. The
second result is false when the request did not include metadata.

declarations.name: Server
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.Server struct{name string; version string; instructions string; tools map[string]*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.Tool; order []string}
declarations.doc: Server is a JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP server that dispatches to registered tools.

methods.name: RegisterTool
methods.doc: RegisterTool adds a tool to the server. Panics on duplicate names.

methods.name: ServeIO
methods.signature: func (*github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.Server).ServeIO(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, w io.Writer) error
methods.doc:
ServeIO runs the server on the given reader and writer. This method is the
primary entry point for testing.

Tool-call requests (tools/call) are dispatched concurrently so that a slow
handler cannot block the read loop or delay responses to subsequent requests.
Non-tool requests (initialize, ping, tools/list) are processed synchronously
because they are fast and their order relative to tool calls is significant.
The method waits for all in-flight tool handlers to complete before
returning, so callers can safely close the writer after ServeIO returns.

methods.name: ServeStdio
methods.doc:
ServeStdio runs the server on os.Stdin/os.Stdout. All logging goes to
os.Stderr to avoid polluting the JSON-RPC transport.

methods.name: SetInstructions
methods.doc:
SetInstructions sets the server-level usage guidance returned to clients in
the "instructions" field of the initialize response. MCP clients typically
surface this text to the model as system context, so it is the primary lever
for telling agents when and how to use the server's tools. An empty string
(the default) omits the field entirely.

declarations.name: Tool
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.Tool struct{Name string; Description string; InputSchema encoding/json.RawMessage; Annotations *github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.ToolAnnotations; Handler func(ctx context.Context, input encoding/json.RawMessage) (any, error)}
declarations.doc: Tool defines a MCP tool that can be called by clients.

fields.name: Annotations
fields.doc:
Annotations carries optional MCP tool-behaviour hints. When nil or
all-zero, no "annotations" field is emitted in tools/list.

fields.name: Handler
fields.doc:
Handler is invoked when the client calls this tool. input is the raw JSON
"arguments" object from the tools/call request. The returned value is
marshalled as the tool result; if err is non-nil the server sends a tool
error response instead.

declarations.name: ToolAnnotations
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.ToolAnnotations struct{Title string "json:\"title,omitempty\""; ReadOnlyHint bool "json:\"readOnlyHint,omitempty\""; IdempotentHint bool "json:\"idempotentHint,omitempty\""; OpenWorldHint bool "json:\"openWorldHint,omitempty\""; DestructiveHint bool "json:\"destructiveHint,omitempty\""}
declarations.doc:
ToolAnnotations carries optional MCP tool-behaviour hints that are
serialised as the standard "annotations" field in tools/list. These are
client-facing advisory hints, not Guard-style enforcement. A nil/zero
value omits the field entirely from the protocol response.

The four hint fields (ReadOnlyHint, IdempotentHint, OpenWorldHint,
DestructiveHint) and their wire names are specified in
contracts/mcp_tool_annotations.json, the cross-language contract the Swift
half (symaira-appkit/SymairaMCP) is implemented against. Every registered
tool should set ReadOnlyHint explicitly: a missing hint is read by
downstream consumers as "write", the least-trusted classification.

fields.name: DestructiveHint
fields.doc:
DestructiveHint, when true, tells the client that this tool may
perform destructive updates (deletes, overwrites, etc.).

fields.name: IdempotentHint
fields.doc:
IdempotentHint, when true, tells the client that calling this tool
repeatedly with the same arguments produces the same result.

fields.name: OpenWorldHint
fields.doc:
OpenWorldHint, when true, tells the client that this tool may
interact with external entities outside the MCP server's control.

fields.name: ReadOnlyHint
fields.doc:
ReadOnlyHint, when true, tells the client that this tool performs no
side-effect state changes.

fields.name: Title
fields.doc: Title is a human-readable title for the tool.

declarations.name: ToolErrorData
declarations.doc:
ToolErrorData renders the structured metadata an error carries into the
object published under [ToolErrorMetaKey]. It returns nil when the error
describes itself no further than its message, which is the signal to omit
"_meta" entirely.

Every interface is consulted with [errors.As], so a wrapped error still
reports the metadata of the error underneath. A [exitcodes.CLIError] fills
in "code" (from its Kind) and "hint" when nothing more specific did.

Boolean fields are reported whenever the error implements their interface,
including when they are false: "retryable": false is a statement that
retrying will not help, which is exactly what a caller needs, while an
absent field only means the error never said.

declarations.name: ToolErrorMetaKey
declarations.doc:
ToolErrorMetaKey is the tool-result "_meta" key under which a failed
tools/call carries the machine-readable twin of its message.

MCP reports a tool failure as a result with isError: true whose content is
prose written for the model. Prose is all a caller gets unless the error
says more about itself, so an agent cannot tell a refused address from a
mistyped selector from a slow host without parsing English — and a server
that wants to deliver a code ends up rendering it into the sentence. The
base MCP Result type carries a free-form "_meta" object (present since
protocol version 2024-11-05); this key holds the structured fields, and
the message text stays exactly what the handler produced.

The key is namespaced per the MCP "_meta" naming rule: a reverse-DNS-style
prefix, a slash, then the name.

declarations.name: ToolResult
declarations.signature: type github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.ToolResult struct{Content []github.com/danieljustus/symaira-corekit/mcpserver.ContentBlock "json:\"content\""; StructuredContent any "json:\"structuredContent,omitempty\""; Meta map[string]any "json:\"_meta,omitempty\""}

packages.name: ollamakit
packages.doc:
Package ollamakit provides a compatibility surface for the shared Ollama
provider in llmkit.

Deprecated: use llmkit directly for new code. This package remains as a thin
shim so existing consumers can migrate without a flag-day API change. All
HTTP requests are delegated to llmkit; no second Ollama transport is kept.

methods.name: Chat

methods.name: Generate

declarations.name: NewFromEnv

NewFromEnv reads <PREFIX>_BASE_URL, <PREFIX>_MODEL and <PREFIX>_TIMEOUT.
